name: ticketise
title: Ticketise
description: Cut a designed or defined product into vertical-slice tickets, written as files then pushed to Linear, Notion, GitHub Issues, or kept on disk.
notes:
## Ticketise

Fourth skill of the Veebee chain (open source, MIT): from a blank page to a shipped product, one skill per step. Takes over from `style` and `define`.

**It cuts, it does not build and it does not plan a calendar.**

- **Reads what exists, best source first**: what came back from a design tool (exported files, images, a link), `style`'s prompt to spot surfaces that were never drawn, `define`'s documents, or plain product instructions when there is nothing else. Never refuses for lack of a design.
- **A ticket is a vertical slice**: one thing a user can do, from the screen to the data, ending in one pull request that can be checked by using it. Never a layer. The first ticket is the thinnest slice crossing the whole product. More than seven acceptance criteria or two journeys, and it is two tickets. Empty states and errors are criteria of their slice.
- **Shows the whole cut first**, numbered with dependencies, and writes nothing until the user says it holds.
- **Names the holes instead of filling them**: a rule no ticket carries, a screen no journey reaches, a feature with no screen.
- **What, and how only when code exists.** On an empty directory a ticket names no framework and no file; in a repository it says where the slice plugs in.
- **Files first, then pushed.** Tickets are written to `.veebee/tickets/` (or the milestone's folder), so they live in git and `ship` reads them without a connector. Then they go to whatever is really connected: Linear, Notion, GitHub Issues. One confirmation with the count and the exact destination before anything is created.
- **A second run is safe**: the tracker id is written back into each file, so tickets are updated, never duplicated, and never deleted in the tracker.
- A live page shows the tickets as cards; the finish prints the project tree read from disk.

Triggers: "fais les tickets", "découpe en tickets", "ticketise", "mets ça dans Linear", "write the tickets", "break this into issues". Not for deciding what the product does: that is `define`.

No secrets, no environment variables: pushing uses the tracker connectors already present in the host agent. Source: https://github.com/The-Vibe-Company/veebee-skills
